boost_if_present.why: Lean on both banks points to a common cause upstream of the cylinders — an intake leak — rather than bank-1-specific fueling.

explanation: The ECU is adding more fuel than expected on bank 1 to hold the target air-fuel mixture. This says the mixture is lean; it does not say which part failed.

initial_hypotheses.label: Exhaust leak ahead of O2 sensor / O2 sensor fault

repairs.label: Inspect the intake system for leaks
repairs.verification: A smoke test or propane-enrichment check that finds the leak confirms the diagnosis before any part is ordered.

repairs.label: Replace intake / PCV hose
repairs.verification: Rescan after repair; fuel trims should return near 0% and P0171 should not return over several drive cycles.

repairs.label: Clean or replace MAF sensor
repairs.verification: Rescan; fuel trims should normalize at idle and cruise, and P0171 should stay clear.

repairs.label: Fuel pressure test, then pump/filter as indicated
repairs.verification: Fuel pressure within spec rules delivery in or out before any fuel part is bought.

safety.stop_message: Stop driving and seek professional service: a safety flag was observed during diagnosis.

conditions.note: Two snapshots, each a 5 s average of 1 Hz samples: one at warm idle, one held at a steady 2500 RPM. trim_idle/trim_2500 are STFT+LTFT (bank 1) in percent.

tests.question: Record combined fuel trim (STFT + LTFT, bank 1) at idle and at a steady 2,500 RPM.

leak_found.label: Visible leak: split hose, disconnected line, or audible hiss

tests.question: Any split hose, disconnected vacuum line, cracked intake duct, or audible hissing around the intake?

title: System too lean, bank 1
